He said: If an had entered into such-and-such, it would have been correct. He said: And its example in speech is: Your example is that you are such-and-such, and that you are such-and-such. And his saying: (So let man look at his food. I) from one perspective, is like the Paradise that the righteous are promised, in it: We poured out the water, the name is clear because it is returned to the food in the accusative, and is renewed, meaning: His food is I poured out, then we did. He said: The meaning of his saying: Like Paradise, is the attributes of Paradise. Some Basran grammarians said: The meaning of this is: the description of Paradise.
He said: And from this is the saying of God Almighty: And to Him belongs the highest description, meaning: To God belongs the highest description. He said: So the meaning of the speech in His saying:
h
The description of Paradise which the righteous have been promised is that rivers flow beneath it

, or rivers in it, is as if he said: The description of Paradise is a description of rivers flow beneath it, or a description of rivers in it, and God knows best. He said: Another aspect, as if it is said: Like Paradise, it is said: Paradise that the righteous are promised. He said: And likewise his saying: And that it is in the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful, as if he said: By God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful, and God knows best. He said: His saying: For what I neglected in the side of God, in the essence of God, as if it was said in our view: in God. He said: And likewise his saying:
h
There is nothing like Him
, the meaning is: He is not like anything and
h
there is nothing like Him
, because He has no equal.

He said: And this is not like your saying to a man: There is no one like you, because it is possible that He has an equal, and by God that is not possible for Him. He said: And similar to it is the saying of Labid: Until the year, then peace be upon you both He said: And he explained to us that he meant: Peace be upon you both. Aws bin Hajar said: And the dead are noble, like trunks, covered by torrential rains. He said: The meaning for us is: like trunks, because he did not want to make a metaphor for trunks, then liken the dead to them. He said: And similar to it is the saying of Umayyah: Saturn and Taurus under his right foot, the Eagle under the other, and a lion under his watch. He said: He said: Under his right foot, as if he said: Under his foot, or under his right foot. He said: And the saying of Labid: I lost his mast and his guest, we roam its matter in the hand of the left As if he said: He ordered her to the north, and to the north, and Labid also said: Even if you throw a hand at an infidel It is as if he said: Until I fell into an infidel.

Another of them said: He is one of those who are blind to his report. He said: The Arabs do that. He said: And it has another meaning: For those who responded to their Lord is the best, like Paradise, a relative pronoun, an attribute for them according to the first statement.

The most correct of the sayings about this is to say: The parable was mentioned, so he said: The parable of Paradise, meaning Paradise, then Paradise was described with its description, and that is because its like is its description, and its description is nothing other than it.

i: Since that was the case, then the parable was mentioned and it was said: The like of Paradise, and its like is its description and the description of Paradise, so its description was like the description of the parable, and it was as if the speech was about mentioning Paradise, so it was said: Paradise has rivers flowing beneath it, as the poet said:
x: I see the years passing by, taking from me as secrets are taken from the crescent moon.
He mentioned the bitterness, and returned in the report to the years. His saying:
h
Its food is permanent and its shade

, meaning what is eaten in it. He says: It is permanent for its people, it does not cease from them, it does not disappear, and it does not perish, but it is fixed without end. And its shade, he says: And its shade is also permanent, because there is no sun in it. This is the outcome of those who fear God, meaning: This is Paradise, which God Almighty described as the outcome of those who fear God, avoid His sins, and perform His obligations. And His saying:
h
And the consequence of the disbelievers is the Fire
, means: And the consequence of the disbelievers in God is the Fire.
God Almighty says: And those to whom We have sent down the Book, who have come to you and followed you, O Muhammad, rejoice in what has been sent down to you of it,
h
And among the parties are those who deny some of it

, meaning: And among the people of the religions who are parties against you, and they are people of various religions, and those who deny some of what has been sent down to you. So say to them: I have only been commanded, O people, to worship God alone, and not to associate anything with Him, and not to associate anything with Him, meaning: I make a partner for Him in my worship, so I worship the gods and idols with Him, rather I sincerely devote my religion to Him, inclining toward truth, To Him I invite, meaning: I invite people to obey Him and sincerely worship Him, and to Him is my return, meaning: And to Him is my destiny. It is a passive participle, from the saying of the speaker: Ab, ya’ub, awab, ma’aba.
And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And those to whom We gave the Scripture rejoice in what has been revealed to you
, those are the companions of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, they rejoiced in the Book of God and in His Messenger and believed in him. His saying:
h
And among the parties are those who deny some of it
, meaning the Jews and Christians.

c: Al-Hasan bin Muhammad told us, he said, Shababah told us, he said, Warqa’ told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And among the parties are those who deny some of it
, he said: Among the People of the Book.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Abdullah told us, on the authority of Warqa’, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: the same.

c: Al-Qasim told us, Al-Husayn told us, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And those to whom We gave the Scripture rejoice in what has been revealed to you

, [O Muhammad], but among the parties are those who deny part of it, of the People of the Scripture, and the parties are the People of the Scripture, and their partisanship brings them closer. And his statement: And if the parties come to him, he said: because of their partisanship against the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. Ibn Jurayj said, and he said on the authority of Mujahid: denies part of it, he said: part of the Qur’an.

c: Muhammad bin Abdul A’la told us, he said, Muhammad bin Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada:
m: And to Him is the return, and to Him is the destination of every servant.

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said
m: regarding His statement,
h
And those to whom We gave the Scripture rejoice in what has been revealed to you

, he said: This is from those who believed in the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, from among the People of the Scripture, so they rejoice in that. And he recited: And among them are those who believe in it and among them are those who do not believe in it. And regarding His statement, And among the parties are those who deny part of it, he said: The parties are the nations, the Jews, Christians, and Magians, among them are those who believed in it and among them are those who denied it.

x: God Almighty says: And just as We sent down the Book to you, O Muhammad, and some of the parties denied it, so also We sent down the judgment and religion, an Arabic judgment, and made that, Arabic, and described it as such, because it was sent down to Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he was an Arab, so the religion was attributed to him, since it was sent down to him, and the parties denied it. Then God Almighty forbade him from abandoning what was sent down to him and following the parties, and threatened him for that if he did so, saying: And if you follow, O Muhammad, their desires, the desires of these parties and their satisfaction and love, and you switched from your religion to their religion, you will have no one to protect you from the punishment of God if He punishes you for following their desires, and you will have no supporter to aid you and rescue you from God if He punishes you, meaning: So beware of following their desires.

God Almighty says: And We have sent, O Muhammad, messengers before you to nations that have passed on before your nation, and We made them human beings like you, with wives to marry, and offspring whom they produced, and We did not make them angels who do not eat, drink, or marry, so that We would make the messenger to your people from the angels like them, but We sent to them human beings like them, just as We sent to those before them from all the nations human beings like them, And it is not for a messenger to bring a sign except by the permission of God, God Almighty says: And it is not possible for a messenger whom God sent to His creation to bring his nation a sign, such as moving mountains, moving a town from one place to another, reviving the dead, and similar signs, except by the permission of God, meaning: except by God’s command to the mountains to move, the earth to move, and the dead to come back to life, For every term is a book, meaning: For every term there is a matter that God has decreed, a book that has been decreed. He wrote it and it is with him.
It has been said: Its meaning is: Every book that God sent down from heaven has a term.
Who said that?

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq bin Yusuf told us, on the authority of Juwaybir, on the authority of Al-Dahhak,
m: regarding his statement: For every term there is a book, he said: For every book that comes down from the sky there is a term, so God erases from it what He wills and confirms, and with Him is the Mother of the Book.

x: This is, according to the saying, similar to the saying of God: And the stupor of death will come with the truth. Abu Bakr, may God have mercy on him, used to recite: And the stupor of truth will come with death, because the stupor of death will come with the truth, and the truth will come with it, so is the appointed time, for it is a book, and for the book there is a appointed time.

The people of interpretation differed in the interpretation of that: Some of them said: God erases whatever He wills of the affairs of His servants and changes it, except for misery and happiness, for they cannot be changed.
Who said that?

c: Abu Kuraib told us, he said, Bahr bin Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Laila, on the authority of Al-Munhal, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement:
h
God blots out what He wills and confirms
h
and with Him is the Mother of the Book
, he said: God manages the matter of worship, and blots out what He wills except misery and happiness, life and death.

c: Ibn Bashar told us, he said, Ibn Abi Laila told us, on the authority of Al-Munhal Ibn Amr, on the authority of Saeed Ibn Jubayr, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement:
h
God blots out what He wills and confirms
h
and with Him is the Mother of the Book
, he said: Everything except happiness and misery, for He has finished with them.

c: Ali bin Sahl told me, he said, Yazid told us, and Ahmad told us, he said, Abu Ahmad told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Ibn Abi Laila, on the authority of Al-Munhal, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said:
m: h
God erases what He wills and confirms
h
and with Him is the Mother of the Book
, he said: Except for misery, death, and life.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Naim Al-Fadl bin Dukayn and Qubaysah told us, they said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Laila, on the authority of Al-Munhal bin Amr, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: the same.

c: Amr bin Ali told us, he said, Wakee’ told us, he said, Ibn Abi Laila told us, on the authority of Al-Munhal bin Amr, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement:
h
God blots out what He wills and confirms
h
and with Him is the Mother of the Book
, he said, Ibn Abbas said: Except for life and death, misery and happiness.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Amr bin Awn told us, he said, Hisham told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Laila, on the authority of Al-Munhal bin Amr, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement:
h
God blots out what He wills and confirms
h
and with Him is the Mother of the Book
, he said: God decrees the affairs of the year on the Night of Decree, except for misery and happiness, death and life.

c: Amr bin Ali told us, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding his statement:
h
God erases what He wills and confirms
, he said: Except for life and death, happiness and misery, for they do not change.

c: Amr told us, he said, Abd al-Rahman told us, he said, Muadh bin Uqbah told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: the same.

c: Ibn Bashar told us, he said, Abu Ahmad told us, he said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: the same. He said, Abu Ahmad told us, he said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Mansur, he said: I said to Mujahid: If you wrote me happy, then confirm me, and if you wrote me miserable, then erase me. He said: Misery and happiness have been completed.

c: Ahmad told us, he said, Abu Ahmad told us, he said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Mujahid - he
m: said, Saeed bin Sulaiman told us, he said, Sharik told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Mujahid:
h
God erases what He wills and confirms
, he said: God sends down everything in the year on the Night of Decree, and erases what He wills of life spans, provisions, and destinies, except for misery and happiness, for they are confirmed.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Jarir told us, on the authority of Mansur, he said,
m: I asked Mujahid and said: What do you think of the supplication of one of us who says: O God, if my name is among the happy ones, then make it among them, and if it is among the wretched ones, then erase it from them and make it among the happy ones? Hassan said: Then I came to him after that a year or more, and asked him about that, and he said: (Indeed, We sent it down during a blessed night. Indeed, We were to warn. * On it is made distinct every matter of wisdom.) He said: On the Night of Decree, whatever provision or calamity will be in the year is decreed, then He advances what He wills and delays what He wills. As for the decree of misery and happiness, it is fixed and does not change.

x: Others said: The meaning of this is that
h
God erases whatever He wills and confirms
from the Book other than the Mother of the Book, in which nothing can be changed.
Who said that?

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Hajjaj told us, he said, Hammad told us, on the authority of Sulayman al-Taymi, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, that he said
m: regarding this verse:
h
God erases whatever He wills and confirms
h
and with Him is the Mother of the Book
, he said: Two books, a book from which He erases whatever He wills and confirms,
h
and with Him is the Mother of the Book

c: Amr bin Ali told us, Sahl bin Yusuf told us, Sulayman al-Taymi told us, on the authority of Ikrimah,
m: regarding his statement:
h
God erases whatever He wills and confirms
h
and with Him is the Mother of the Book
, he said: The Book is two books: a book from which
h
God erases whatever He wills and confirms
h
and with Him is the Mother of the Book
. He said, Abu Amer told us, Hammad bin Salamah told us, on the authority of Sulayman al-Taymi, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, similarly.

c: Muhammad bin Abdul A’la told us, he said, Al-Mu’tamir bin Sulayman told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ikrimah, he said:
m: The Book is two books,
h
God erases what He wills and confirms
h
and with Him is the Mother of the Book

x: Others said: Rather, the meaning of this is that He erases whatever He wills and confirms whatever He wants.
Who said that?

c: Abu Kuraib told us, he said, Othman told us, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Shuqaiq,
m: that he used to say: O God, if you have written us as miserable, then erase us and write us as happy, and if you have written us as happy, then confirm us, for you erase what you will and confirm, and with you is the Mother of the Book.

c: Amr told us, he said, Wakee’ told us, he said, Al-A’mash told us, on the authority of Abu Wa’il, he said:
m: Among the things that he often used to supplicate with were these words: O God, if you have written us as miserable, then erase us and write us as happy, and if you have written us as happy, then make us steadfast, for you erase what you will and make steadfast, and with you is the Mother of the Book. He said, Muadh bin Hisham told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Abu Hakima, on the authority of Abu Uthman al-Nahdi: That Umar bin al-Khattab said while he was circumambulating the House and crying: O God, if You have written for me misery or sin, then erase it, for You erase what You will and confirm, and with You is the Mother of the Book, so make it happiness and forgiveness. He said, Mu’tamir told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abu Hakima, on the authority of Abu Uthman. He said: I think I heard it from Abu Uthman, similarly. He said, Abu Amer told us, he said, Qara bin Khalid told us, on the authority of Asma Abu Hakima, on the authority of Abu Uthman al-Nahdi, on the authority of Umar, may God have mercy on him, the same.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Al-Hajjaj told us, he said, Hammad told us, he said, Abu Hakima told us, he said:
m: I heard Abu Uthman Al-Nahdi say: I heard Umar ibn Al-Khattab, may God be pleased with him, say, while he was circumambulating the Kaaba: O God, if you have written me among the people of happiness, then confirm me in it, and if you have written for me sin and misery, then erase me and confirm me among the people of happiness, for you erase what you will and confirm, and with you is the Mother of the Book. He said, Al-Hajjaj bin Al-Munhal told us, he said, Hammad told us, on the authority of Khalid Al-Hadha’, on the authority of Abu Qilabah, on the authority of Ibn Masoud, that he used to say: O God, if you have written me among the people of misery, then erase me and establish me among the people of happiness.

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement:
h
God blots out what He wills and confirms
h
and with Him is the Mother of the Book

, meaning: He is the man who spends his time obeying God, then returns to disobeying God and dies in his misguidance, so he is the one who blots out. And the one who confirms: The man who commits a sin in disobedience to God, and he had previously done good, until he dies in obedience to God, so he is the one who confirms.

c: Ahmad told us, Abu Ahmad told us, Sharik told us, on the authority of Hilal bin Hamid, on the authority of Abdullah bin Ukaim, on the authority of Abdullah
m: that he used to say: O God, if you have written me among the happy ones, then confirm me among the happy ones, for you erase what you will and confirm, and with you is the Mother of the Book.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Al-Hajjaj told us, he said, Hammad told us, on the authority of Abu Hamza, on the authority of Ibrahim:
m: That Kaab said to Umar, may God have mercy on him: O Commander of the Faithful, were it not for a verse in the Book of God, I would have informed you of what will happen until the Day of Resurrection. He said: What is it? He said: The statement of God:
h
God blots out what He wills and confirms
h
and with Him is the Mother of the Book

c: It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn,
m: who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubayd told us, who said: I heard Ad-Dahhak say regarding His statement: For every term is a book, the verse, he said:
h
God erases what He wills
, he said: I abrogate what I will, and I do from the actions what I will, if I will I will increase them, and if I will I will decrease them.

c: Al-Hasan bin Muhammad told us, Affan told us, Hammam told us, Al-Kalbi told us,
m: God erases and confirms whatever He wills, he said: He erases from provision and increases it, and erases from life span and increases it. I said: Who told you that? He said: Abu Salih, on the authority of Jabir bin Abdullah bin Ri’ab Al-Ansari, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. Then Al-Kalbi came forward and was asked about this verse: God Surat al-Ra'd 13:39 God blots out whatever He wills and confirms,
h
and with Him is the Mother of the Book

. erases and confirms whatever He wills, he said: He writes down the entire statement, until Thursday comes, and everything that does not have a reward or punishment is removed from it, such as your saying: I ate, I drank, I entered, I left, and similar statements, and they are true, and what has a reward or punishment is confirmed.

c: Al-Hasan told us, he said, Abdul-Wahhab told us, he said,
m: I heard Al-Kalbi, on the authority of Abu Salih, something similar, and he did not go beyond Abu Salih.

x: Others said: Rather, the meaning of this is that God abrogates whatever He wills of the rulings of His Book, and confirms whatever He wills of them, but He does not abrogate them.
Who said that?

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abdullah bin Saleh told us, he said, Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: h
God erases what He wills
, he said: of the Qur’an. He says: God changes what He wills and abrogates it, and confirms what He wills and does not change it.
h
And with Him is the Mother of the Book
, he says: The sum of that is with Him in the Mother of the Book, the abrogating and the abrogated, what is changed and what is confirmed, all of that is in a book.

c: Bishr told us, Yazid told us, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement:
h
God erases what He wills and confirms
, is like his statement:
h
Whatever verse We abrogate or cause to be forgotten
, We bring forth [one] better than it or similar to it, and his statement:
h
And with Him is the Mother of the Book
, meaning the entirety of the Book and its origin.

c: Muhammad ibn Abd al-A’la told us, he said, Muhammad ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada:
m: h
God erases what He wills and confirms
, what He wills, and He is the Wise,
h
and with Him is the Mother of the Book
, and its origin.

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said
m: regarding His statement,
h
God erases what He wills
, that is, what He sends down to the prophets, and confirms, that is, what He wills of what He sends down to the prophets, he said,
h
and with Him is the Mother of the Book
, that is, He does not change or alter.

c: Al-Qasim told us, Al-Hussein told us, Hajjaj told me, Ibn Jurayj said:
m: h
God erases what He wills
, he said: He abrogates. He said:
h
And with Him is the Mother of the Book
, he said: The Reminder.

x: Others said: The meaning of this is that he erases those whose time has come, and confirms those whose time has not yet come.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Bashar told us, he said, Ibn Abi Uday told us, on the authority of Awf, on the authority of Al-Hasan,
m: regarding his statement:
h
God erases what He wills and confirms
h
and with Him is the Mother of the Book
, he says: He erases whoever’s time has come and gone, and what is confirmed is the one who is alive and continues to his time.

c: Amr bin Ali told us, Yahya told us, Aouf told us:
m: I heard Al-Hasan say:
h
God erases what He wills
, he said: whoever has reached his appointed time, and confirms, he said: whoever has not reached his appointed time.

c: Al-Hasan bin Muhammad told us, he said, Hudha told us, he said, Aouf told us, on the authority of Al-Hasan,
m: similar to the hadith of Ibn Bashar. He said, Abd al-Wahhab ibn Ata’ told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of al-Hasan, regarding his statement: For every term there is a book, he said: The terms of the children of Adam are in a book, God erases their terms and confirms them,
h
and with Him is the Mother of the Book
. He said, Shababah told us, Warqa’ told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding the statement of God:
h
God blots out what He wills and confirms

, the Quraysh said when the verse was revealed: And it is not for a messenger to bring a sign except by permission of God: We do not see you, O Muhammad, having control over anything, and the matter has already been completed! So this verse was revealed to frighten and warn them: If We will, We can innovate for him from Our affair whatever We will, and we innovate every Ramadan, so we blot out and confirm whatever We will of the people’s provisions and their calamities, and what We give them, and what We apportion to them.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Abdullah told us, on the authority of Warqa’, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: something similar.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Hussein told us, he said, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: something similar.

x: Others said: The meaning of this is: He forgives whatever sins He wills of His servants, and leaves whatever He wills and does not forgive.
Who said that?

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Hakam told us, on the authority of Amr, on the authority of Ata’, on the authority of Saeed,
m: regarding his statement:
h
God erases what He wills and confirms
, he said: He confirms in the stomach misery and happiness, and everything, so He forgives from it what He wills, and delays what He wills.

x: The most correct and most correct of the statements that were mentioned regarding the interpretation of the verse is the statement that we mentioned from Al-Hasan and Mujahid, and that is that God, the Most High, threatened the polytheists who asked the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, for signs with punishment, and warned them with it, and said to them: (And it is not for a messenger to bring a sign except by God’s permission. For every term is a decree), informing them with that that His judgment concerning them has a decree established in a decree, and they are postponed until the time of the coming of that decree. Then He said to them: When that decree comes, God will bring whomever He wills of those whose term has drawn near and whose provision has been cut off, or whose death has come, or whose humiliation has come from being exalted, or whose wealth has been lost, and He will decree that for His creation, and that is its erasure, and He will confirm whatever He wills of those whose term, provision, and food remain, and He will leave them as they are and not erase them.
In this sense, the hadith of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, came, which is:

c: Muhammad ibn Sahl ibn Askar told me, he said, Ibn Abi Maryam told us, he said, Al-Layth ibn Saad told us, on the authority of Ziyadah ibn Muhammad, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Ka’b Al-Qurazi, on the authority of Fadala ibn Ubayd, on the authority of Abu Al-Darda’, he said:
m: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “God opens the remembrance in the three hours remaining of the night. In the first hour of them He looks in the book which no one else looks at, so He erases what He wills and confirms.” Then he mentioned what is in the last two hours.

c: Musa bin Sahl al-Ramli told us, he said, Adam told us, he said, al-Layth told us, he said, Ziyadah bin Muhammad told us, on the authority of Muhammad bin Ka’b al-Qurazi, on the authority of Fadala bin Ubayd, on the authority of Abu al-Darda’, he said:
m: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: God descends during the three hours remaining of the night, and He opens the remembrance in the first hour that no one else has seen, He erases what He wills and confirms what He wills.

c: Muhammad bin Sahl bin Askar told me, he said, Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said, Ibn Jurayj told us, on the authority of Ata’, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said:
m: God has a preserved tablet that is five hundred years long, made of white pearl with two covers of ruby, and the two covers are two tablets of God, every day three hundred and sixty moments, He erases what He wills and confirms,
h
and with Him is the Mother of the Book

c: Muhammad bin Abdul A’la told us, he said, Muhammad bin Thawr told us, he said, Al-Mu’tamir bin Sulayman told us, on the authority of his father, he said, a man told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Qais bin Ibad, that he said:
m: The tenth of Rajab is a day on which God erases whatever He wills.

x: The statement in the interpretation of the Almighty’s saying:
h
And with Him is the Mother of the Book
The people of interpretation differed in the interpretation of his saying:
h
And with Him is the Mother of the Book
Some of them said: It means: He has what is permissible and what is forbidden.
Who said that?

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Muslim bin Ibrahim told us, he said, Muhammad bin Uqbah told us, he said, Malik bin Dinar told us, he said:
m: I asked Al-Hasan, I said: The Mother of the Book, he said: The lawful and the unlawful. He said: I said to him: What is Al-Hamdulillah, Lord of the Worlds? He said: This is the Mother of the Qur’an.

x: Others said: Its meaning is: He has the entire book and its origin.
Who said that?

c: Bishr narrated to us, he said, Yazid narrated to us, he said, Saeed narrated to us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And with Him is the Mother of the Book
, he said: The entirety of the Book and its origin.

c: Muhammad bin Abdul-A’la told us, he said, Muhammad bin Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada,
m: the same.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn,
m: who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubayd told us, who said: I heard Al-Dahhak say regarding His statement:
h
And with Him is the Mother of the Book
, he said: A book with the Lord of the Worlds.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq bin Yusuf told us, on the authority of Juwaybir, on the authority of Al-Dahhak:
m: h
And with Him is the Mother of the Book
, he said: The entirety of the Book and its knowledge. He means by that what is abrogated from it and what is confirmed.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Salih told us, he said, Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: h
And with Him is the Mother of the Book
, he says: And the sum of that is with Him in the Mother of the Book, the abrogating and the abrogated, what is replaced and what is confirmed, all of that is in a book.

x: Others said about this:

c: Al-Qasim told us, Al-Hussein told us, Mu’tamir bin Sulayman told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Sayyar, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: that he asked Ka’b about the Mother of the Book. He said: God’s knowledge, what He created, and what He created, He works. So He said to His knowledge: Be a book, and it was a book.

x: Others said: It is the male.
Who said that?

c: Al-Qasim told us, Al-Hussein told us, Hajjaj told me, Abu Jaʿfar said:
m: I do not know whether Ibn Jurayj is in it or not. He said: Ibn Abbas said:
h
And with Him is the Mother of the Book
, he said: The Reminder.

x: The most correct of the sayings on this matter is the saying of the one who said: And with Him is the origin of the Book and its entirety. This is because the Most High, mentioned above, informed us that He erases whatever He wills and confirms whatever He wills, then He followed that with His saying:
h
And with Him is the Mother of the Book
, so it was clear that its meaning is: And with Him is the Surat al-Ra'd 13:39 God blots out whatever He wills and confirms,
h
and with Him is the Mother of the Book
. origin of what is confirmed and what is erased and its entirety in a book with Him.

There is a difference in the reading of his saying: And it is established. This was read by most of the people of Medina and Kufa: And he affirms with a shaddah on the ba, meaning: And he leaves it and keeps it as it is, and does not erase it. Some Meccans, some Basrans, and some Kufians read it as and establishes, with a light pronunciation, meaning: writes. We have previously explained that the meaning of this, according to us, is: his written approval and leaving it to be erased, as we have explained. If this is the case, then confirming it is more appropriate, and emphasis is more correct than alleviation, even though alleviation may be interpreted in meaning as emphasis, and emphasis as alleviation, because their meanings are similar. As for erasure, the Arabs have two dialects for it: As for Mudar, they say: I erased the book, I erase it, erasure, and with it the revelation, and I erased it, I erased it, erasure.
It was mentioned about some of the Rabi’ah tribes that they say: I erased, I erased.

evidence.text: Abu Jaafar said: There is a difference in the reading of his saying: And it is established.
This was read by most of the people of Medina and Kufa: And he affirms with a shaddah on the ba, meaning: And he leaves it and keeps it as it is, and does not erase it.
Some Meccans, some Basrans, and some Kufians read it as and establishes, with a light pronunciation, meaning: writes.

x: God Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: Either We show you, O Muhammad, during your lifetime some of the punishment We promise these polytheists for their disbelief, or We cause you to die before We show you that. You only have to obey your Lord in what He has commanded you to do in conveying His message to them, not seeking their goodness or their corruption. It is up to Us to hold them accountable, and to reward them for their deeds, if good then good, and if evil then evil.
The interpreters differed in their interpretation of that.

Some of them said: Its meaning is: Did not these polytheists from the people of Mecca who asked Muhammad for signs see that we would come to the land and open it for him, land after land, around their land? Do they not fear that we would open their land for him as we opened others for him?
Who said that?

c: Al-Hasan bin Muhammad told us, he said, Muhammad bin Al-Sabah told us, he said, Hisham told us, on the authority of Hisin, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement:
h
We come to the land
, reducing it from its borders, he said: Did they not see that We open up land after land for Muhammad?

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement:
h
Have they not seen that We come to the land and reduce it from its borders
? He means by that what God opened for Muhammad. He says: That is its reduction.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Salamah bin Nabit, on the authority of Ad-Dahhak, he said:
m: What you conquered from the enemy’s land.

c: Muhammad bin Abdul A’la told us, he said, Muhammad bin Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, he said:
m: Al-Hasan used to say regarding His statement:
h
Have they not seen that We come to the land
, reducing it from its borders, it is the victory of the Muslims over the polytheists.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn,
m: who said: I heard Abu Muadh, who said: Ubayd ibn Sulayman narrated to us, who said: I heard Ad-Dahhak say regarding His statement:
h
Have they not seen that We come to the land

, reducing it from its borders? He meant that the land around him was being reduced for the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. They looked at that but did not take heed. God said in Surat al-Anbiya 21:“
h
We come to the land
, reducing it from its borders. So are they the victors?” Rather, the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and his companions are the victors.

x: Others said: Rather, its meaning is: Did they not see that
h
we come to the land
and destroy it, or are they not afraid that we will do the same to them and their land, so that we will destroy them and destroy their land?
Who said that?

c: Al-Hasan bin Muhammad told us, he said, Ali bin Asim told us, on the authority of Hissain bin Abd al-Rahman, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement:
h
We come to the land

, reducing it from its borders, he said: Did they not see the village being destroyed until the population was on one side? He said, Hajjaj bin Muhammad told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Al-A’raj: that he heard Mujahid say:
h
We come to the land
and reduce it from its edges, he said: its devastation.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Hussein told us, he said, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Al-A’raj, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: similarly. He said: And Ibn Jurayj said: Its destruction and the destruction of the people.

c: Ahmad told us, he said, Abu Ahmad told us, he said, Israel told us, on the authority of Abu Jaʿfar al-Farraʿ, on the authority of ʿIkrimah,
m: regarding his statement:
h
Have they not seen that We come to the land and reduce it from its borders
? He said: We destroy it from its borders.

x: Others said: Rather, its meaning is: We reduce its blessings, its fruits, and its people through death.
Who said that?

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abdullah told us, he said, Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement: We will reduce it from its borders, meaning: the reduction of its people and its blessings.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Jarir told us, on the authority of Laith, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding his statement:
h
We reduce it from its borders
, he said: in the souls, in the fruits, and in the destruction of the land.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Talha Al-Qannad, on the authority of someone
m: who heard Al-Sha’bi say: If the earth were decreasing, your house would be cramped for you, but the souls and fruits are decreasing.

x: Others said: Its meaning is:
h
We come to the land
and reduce its people, and we destroy them by taking them to death.
Who said that?

c: Al-Hasan bin Muhammad told us, he said, Shababah told us, he said, Warqa’ told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: We will reduce Surat al-Ra'd 13:41
h
Have they not seen that We come to the land
, reducing it from its borders?
h
And God judges
, and there is no adjuster of His judgment,
h
and He is swift in reckoning
. it from its edges, he said: the death of its people.

c: Ibn Bashar told us, he said, Yahya told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: h
Have they not seen that We come to the land and reduce it from its borders
? He said: Death.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Muslim bin Ibrahim told us, he said, Harun al-Nahwi told us, he said, al-Zubayr bin al-Kharit told us, on the authority of Ikrimah,
m: regarding his statement:
h
We reduce it from its borders
, he said: It is death. Then he said: If the earth were to decrease, we would not find a place to sit in.

c: Muhammad bin Abdul A’la told us, he said, Muhammad bin Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada:
m: h
We come to the land
, reducing it from its borders. He said: Ikrimah used to say: It is the taking of people.

c: Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, he said:
m: Ikrimah was asked about the decrease in the earth, he said: The people’s death.

c: Al-Harith told me, he said, Abdul Aziz told us, he said, Jarir bin Hazim told us, on the authority of Yaʿla bin Hakim, on the authority of Ikrimah,
m: regarding his statement:
h
Have they not seen that We come to the land
, reducing it from its borders? He said: If it were as they say, none of you would have found a well to defecate in.

c: Al-Fadl bin Al-Sabah told us, he said, Ismail bin Aliyah told us, on the authority of Abu Raja’, he said:
m: Ikrimah was asked, while I was listening, about this verse:
h
Have they not seen that We come to the land and reduce it from its borders
? He said: Death.

x: Others said: We will reduce it from its edges, with the departure of its jurists and its elite.
Who said that?

c: Ahmad bin Ishaq told us, Abu Ahmad told us, Talha bin Amr told us, on the authority of Ata’, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said:
m: The departure of its scholars, jurists, and the best of its people. He said, Abu Ahmad told us, he said, Abdul Wahhab told us, on the authority of Mujahid, he said: The death of scholars.

x: The most correct interpretation of this is that of the one who said:
h
Have they not seen that We come to the land

, reducing it from its borders? with the appearance of the Muslims from the companions of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, on it and their subjugation of its people? Will they not take heed of that and fear their appearance on their land and their subjugation of them? That is because God threatened those who asked His Messenger for signs from among the polytheists of his people with His saying: “We shall only show you some of what We promise them, or We shall take you in death. For upon you is only the conveyance, and upon Us is the reckoning.” Then He, the Most High, rebuked them for their poor consideration of what they witness of God’s actions with their peers from the disbelievers, and they still ask for signs, so He said:
h
Have they not seen that We come to the land
, reducing it from its borders? with the subjugation of its people and their dominance over it from its borders and sides, and they do not take heed of what they see of that.
As for his saying:
h
And God judges

, and there is no objection to His judgment, he says: And God is the One who judges, so His judgment is implemented, and He decrees, so His judgment is carried out. And if these polytheists from the people of Mecca bring God’s judgment and His judgment, they will not be able to reject it. What he means by his saying: There is no one to question His judgment, is that there is no one to reverse His judgment. In Arabic, the follower is the one who repeats something. And His saying:
h
And He is swift in reckoning
, means: And God is swift in reckoning, He counts the deeds of these polytheists, nothing is hidden from Him, and He is behind their recompense for them.

God Almighty says: Those who came before these polytheists from Quraysh from the nations that preceded them plotted against the prophets and messengers of God, To God belongs all plotting, meaning: To God belong all the causes of plotting, and in His hand and to Him. The plotting of those who plotted among them does not harm anyone except those whom He wills to harm. He says: So the plotters did not harm with their plotting except those whom God willed to be harmed by it, and they only harmed themselves by it, because they angered their Lord with themselves by doing so, until He destroyed them and saved His messengers. He says: So these polytheists from Quraysh plot against you, O Muhammad, and God is the One who saves you from their plotting, and the One who causes the harm of their plotting to befall them, not you. And His statement:
h
He knows what every soul earns

, meaning: Your Lord knows, O Muhammad, what these polytheists among your people do, and what they strive to do to deceive you, and He knows all the deeds of all creation, nothing of it is hidden from Him.

And the disbelievers will come to know for whom is the final home, meaning: And they will come to know, when they come before their Lord on the Day of Resurrection, for whom is the final home when they enter the Fire, and the believers in God and His Messenger will enter Paradise.

The reading of this differed: So I read it as the people of Medina and some of Basra read: And the disbeliever will know, on the basis of monotheism. As for the Kufa reading, they read it: And the disbelievers will know, in the plural.

The correct reading in this regard is to read for all: And the disbelievers will know, because the report before that was about their group, and after it was followed by report about them, and that is His statement: We will only show you some of what We promise them, or We will cause you to die, and after that His statement: And those who disbelieve will say, ‘You are not a messenger.’ It has been mentioned that in the reading of Ibn Masʿud it is: And the disbelievers will know, and in the reading of Abu it is: And those who disbelieve will know. All of this is evidence of the correctness of what we have chosen from the reading in this regard.

evidence.text: Abu Jaafar said: The reading of this differed: So I read it as the people of Medina and some of Basra read: And the disbeliever will know, on the basis of monotheism.
As for the Kufa reading, they read it: And the disbelievers will know, in the plural.

Abu Jaʿfar said: The correct reading in this regard is to read for all: And the disbelievers will know, because the report before that was about their group, and after it was followed by report about them, and that is His statement: We will only show you some of what We promise them, or We will cause you to die, and after that His statement: And those who disbelieve will say, ‘You are not a messenger.’
It has been mentioned that in the reading of Ibn Masʿud it is: And the disbelievers will know, and in the reading of Abu it is: And those who disbelieve will know.
All of this is evidence of the correctness of what we have chosen from the reading in this regard.

x: God Almighty says: And those who disbelieve in God among your people say, O Muhammad: You are not a messenger! As a denial of you and rejection of your prophethood, then say to them when they say that: God is sufficient, meaning: Say, God is sufficient for me, “as a witness,” meaning: a witness, between me and you, over me and you, of my truthfulness and your falsehood, and with Him is knowledge of the Book. So, if the word man is read in this way, it is in the accusative case, in apposition to the name of God. And the people of the regions read it in this way, meaning: and those who have knowledge of the Book, meaning the books that were revealed before the Qur’an, such as the Torah and the Gospel. And the commentators interpreted it based on this reading.
The narrator mentioned that:

c: Ali bin Saeed Al-Kindi told me, he said, Abu Muhayyah Yahya bin Ya’la told us, on the authority of Abdul Malik bin Umair, on the authority of my nephew Abdullah bin Salam, he said, Abdullah bin Salam said:
m: It was revealed regarding: Sufficient is God as a witness between me and you, and whoever has knowledge of the Book.

c: Al-Husayn bin Ali Al-Sada’i told us, Abu Dawud Al-Tayalisi told us, Shu’ayb bin Safwan told us, Abdul Malik bin Umair told us:
m: Muhammad bin Yusuf bin Abdullah bin Salam said, Abdullah bin Salam said: It was revealed about: “Say: Sufficient is God as a witness between me and you, and whoever has knowledge of the Book.”

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement: Say, ‘Sufficient is God as a witness between me and you, and whoever has knowledge of the Book.’ So those who have knowledge of the Book are the People of the Book from among the Jews and Christians.

c: Abu Kuraib told us, he said, Al-Ashja’i told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Laith, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: h
And with him is knowledge of the Book
, he said: He is Abdullah bin Salam.

c: Yaqub bin Ibrahim told me, he said, Hisham told us, he said, Ismail bin Abi Khalid told us, on the authority of Abu Salih,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And with him is knowledge of the Book
, he said: A man from among mankind, and he did not name him.

c: Al-Hasan bin Muhammad told us, he said, Shababah told us, he said, Warqa’ told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And with him is knowledge of the Book
, he is Abdullah bin Salam. He said, Yahya bin Abbad told us, he said, Shu’bah told us, on the authority of Al-Hakam, on the authority of Mujahid: And whoever has knowledge of the Book...

c: Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: his statement:
h
And those who disbelieve say

, ‘You are not a messenger,’ he said: the statement of the polytheists of Quraysh, Say, ‘Sufficient is God as a witness between me and you, and whoever has knowledge of the Book,’ people from the People of the Book who bore witness to the truth and acknowledged it, and knew that Muhammad was the Messenger of God, as it is reported that among them was Abdullah bin Salam.

c: Muhammad bin Abdul A’la told us, he said, Muhammad bin Thawr told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: And he who has knowledge of the Book, he said: Among them were Abdullah bin Salam, Salman al-Farsi, and Tamim al-Dari.

c: Al-Hasan told us, he said, Abdul-Wahhab told us, on the authority of Saeed, on the authority of Qatada:
m: h
And with him is knowledge of the Book

, he said: He is Abdullah bin Salam. It was mentioned that a group of the ancients used to read it: And with Him is knowledge of the Book, meaning: with God is knowledge of the Book. It was mentioned by those who mentioned that about him:

c: Al-Hasan bin Muhammad told us, he said, Abdul-Wahhab bin Ata’ told us, on the authority of Harun, on the authority of Ja’far bin Abi Wahshiyya, on the authority of Sa’id bin Jubayr, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: And with him is the knowledge of the Book, he says, From God is the knowledge of the Book.

c: Muhammad bin Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Muhammad bin Jaʿfar told us, on the authority of Shuʿbah, on the authority of Al-Hakam, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: And with Him is knowledge of the Book, he said: From God. He said, Ibn Abi Uday told us, on the authority of Shuʿbah, on the authority of Al-Hakam, on the authority of Mujahid: And with Him is the knowledge of the Book, he said: From God is the knowledge of the Book. And this hadith was told to us by Al-Hasan bin Muhammad, he said:

c: Shababah told us, he said: Shuʿbah told us, on the authority of Al-Hakam, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: and with Him is the knowledge of the Book, he said: He is God. This is how Al-Hasan Surat al-Ra'd 13:43
h
And those who disbelieve say

, "You are not a messenger." Say, "Sufficient is God as a witness between me and you, and whoever has knowledge of the Book." read: And with Him is the knowledge of the Book. He said, Shuʿbah told us, on the authority of Mansur bin Zadhan, on the authority of Al-Hasan, the same. He said, Ali told us - meaning Ibn al-Jaʿd - he said, Shuʿbah told us, on the authority of Mansur Ibn Zadhan, on the authority of al-Hasan: And whoever has knowledge of the Book. He said: God. Shuʿbah said: So I mentioned that to al-Hakam, and he said: Mujahid said something similar.

c: Ibn Al-Muthanna told us, he said, Muhammad Ibn Jaʿfar told us, he said, Shuʿbah told us, he said,
m: I heard Mansur Ibn Zadhan narrating, on the authority of Al-Hasan, that he said regarding this verse: And with Him is knowledge of the Book, he said: From God. He said, Al-Hasan bin Muhammad told us, he said, Hudha told us, he said, Aouf told us, on the authority of Al-Hasan: And with him is the knowledge of the Book, he said: From God is the knowledge of the Book.

c: Muhammad ibn Abd al-A’la told us, he said, Muhammad ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of al-Hasan:
m: And whoever has knowledge of the Book, he said: From God is knowledge of the Book. This is what Ibn Abd al-A’la said.

c: Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, he said:
m: Al-Hasan used to recite it: Say, Sufficient is God as a witness between me and you, and whoever has knowledge of the Book, meaning: From God is the knowledge of the Book and its entirety.

c: This is how Bishr told us:
m: the knowledge of the Book, and I think he made a mistake in it, and that it is: and whoever has knowledge of the Book, because his saying: and its entirety, is a noun, and a noun is not conjoined with a past-tense verb.

c: Al-Hasan told us, he said, Abdul-Wahhab told us, on the authority of Harun:
m: And with him is the knowledge of the Book, he says: From God is the knowledge of the Book.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Al-Hajjaj bin Al-Munhal told us, he said, Abu Awana told us, on the authority of Abu Bishr, he said:
m: I said to Saeed bin Jubair:
h
And with him is knowledge of the Book
, is he Abdullah bin Salam? He said: This Surah is Meccan, so how could it be Abdullah bin Salam! He said: And he used to recite it:
h
And with him is knowledge of the Book
, he said: From God.

c: Al-Hasan told us, he said, Saeed bin Mansour told us, he said, Abu Awana told us, on the authority of Abu Bishr, he said:
m: I asked Saeed bin Jubair about the statement of God:
h
And with him is knowledge of the Book
, is he Abdullah bin Salam? He said: That is sufficient, and this Surah is Meccan? And Saeed used to recite it:
h
And with him is knowledge of the Book

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Hussein told us, he said, Ibad told me, on the authority of Awf, on the authority of Al-Hasan,
m: and Juwaybir, on the authority of Al-Dahhak bin Muzahim, he said: And whoever has knowledge of the Book, he said: From God.

x: It has been narrated from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, that this reading and this interpretation are correct, but there is a problem with its chain of transmission, and that is what:

c: Al-Qasim told us, Al-Hussein told us, Ibad bin Al-Awam told me, on the authority of Harun bin Al-Awar, on the authority of Al-Zuhri, on the authority of Salim bin Abdullah, on the authority of his father, on the authority of the Prophet,
m: may God bless him and grant him peace, that he recited: And whoever has knowledge of the Book, with God is knowledge of the Book.

x: This is a report that has no basis among the trustworthy companions of Al-Zuhri. Since that is the case, and the reading of the regions of the people of Hijaz, Syria, and Iraq was based on the other reading, which is: And with Him is knowledge of the Book, then the interpretation that is based on the meaning that the reading of the regions is based on is more deserving of being correct than what contradicts it, since the reading according to what they agreed upon is more deserving of being correct.

evidence.text: So, if the word man is read in this way, it is in the accusative case, in apposition to the name of God.
And the people of the regions read it in this way, meaning: and those who have knowledge of the Book, meaning the books that were revealed before the Qur’an, such as the Torah and the Gospel.
And the commentators interpreted it based on this reading.
It was mentioned that a group of the ancients used to read it: And with Him is knowledge of the Book, meaning: with God is knowledge of the Book.

Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, he said: Al-Hasan used to recite it: Say, Sufficient is God as a witness between me and you, and whoever has knowledge of the Book, meaning: From God is the knowledge of the Book and its entirety.
He said: And he used to recite it: And with him is knowledge of the Book, he said: From God.
And Saeed used to recite it: And with him is knowledge of the Book.

Abu Jaafar said: It has been narrated from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, that this reading and this interpretation are correct, but there is a problem with its chain of transmission, and that is what:

Since that is the case, and the reading of the regions of the people of Hijaz, Syria, and Iraq was based on the other reading, which is: And with Him is knowledge of the Book, then the interpretation that is based on the meaning that the reading of the regions is based on is more deserving of being correct than what contradicts it, since the reading according to what they agreed upon is more deserving of being correct.

notes.en: M reads: “I was embarrassed.” Ḥashamah means modesty and reserve. Al-Aṣmaʿī said: “There is ḥashūm in his hands,” meaning restraint. See Lisān al-ʿArab, root ḥ-sh-m.
notes.ar: في م: "أحشمت". والحشمة: الحياء والانقباض، وقال الأصمعى: في يديه حشوم، أي انقباض. ينظر اللسان (ح ش م).

notes.en: Mā umirru wa-mā uḥlā means: “I will not bring you any word or deed, bitter or sweet.” Lisān al-ʿArab, root m-r-r.
notes.ar: ما أُمِرُّ وما أُحلى، أي: ما آتى بكلمة ولا فَعْلة مرة ولا حلوة. اللسان (م ر ر).

notes.en: Ṣ, T1, T2, S, and F read: “to him.”
notes.ar: في ص، ت 1، ت 2، س، ف: "إليه".

notes.en: M reads: “you wicked one.”
notes.ar: في م: "يا خبيث".

notes.en: M reads: “ablakh.” Ablakh means imposing in his own eyes, daring in the obscenity he commits. Lisān al-ʿArab, root b-l-kh.
notes.ar: في م: "أملخ"، والأبلخ: العظيم في نفسه، الجرئ على ما أتى من الفجور. اللسان (ب ل خ).

notes.en: Rāma, yarīmu means “to depart.” Mā rimtu al-makāna wa-mā rimtu minhu means “I did not leave the place.” See Lisān al-ʿArab, root r-w-m.
notes.ar: رام، يريم: إذا برح، ومارمت المكان وما رمت منه: أي ما برحته. ينظر اللسان (ر و م).

notes.en: M reads: “I struck.”
notes.ar: في م: "ضربت".

notes.en: Ṣ is undotted and reads: “ʿAdiyyah”; M: “ʿAdhiyyah”; T2, S, and F: “ʿAdiyyah.” ʿAdanah is a place in Najd, north of al-Shurbah. Muʿjam al-buldān 3/623.
notes.ar: في ص: "عدية" غير منقوطة، وفى م: "عذية"، وفى ت 2 س، ف: "عدية". وعَدَنة: موضع بنجد في جهة الشمال من الشربة. معجم البلدان 3/ 623.

notes.en: Al-Raqam, with fatḥah on its first two letters, is a place in the Ḥijāz near Wādī al-Qurā. Muʿjam mā istaʿjam 2/666.
notes.ar: الرَّقَم، بفتح أوله وثانيه: موضع بالحجاز، قريب من وادى القرى. معجم ما استعجم 2/ 666.

notes.en: Al-Jurayr is a place in Najd. Muʿjam mā istaʿjam 2/380.
notes.ar: الجُرَير: موضع بنجد. معجم ما استعجم 2/ 380.

notes.en: Ṣ, T2, S, and F read: “al-Bukayr”; T1: “the camel.” Bakr is a young camel. Lisān al-ʿArab, root b-k-r.
notes.ar: في ص، ت 2، س، ف: "البكير"، وفى ت 1: "البعير". والبَكر: ولد الناقة. اللسان (ب ك ر).

notes.en: Ṣ, T1, T2, S, and F read: “he said.”

notes.en: Ḥatf means death; its plural is ḥutūf. Lisān al-ʿArab, root ḥ-t-f.
notes.ar: الحتف: الموت، وجمعه حتوف. اللسان (ح ت ف).

notes.en: Al-Simāk is a well-known star. Nawʾ is a star as it sets. In pre-Islamic times people would say: “Rain came to us with the setting of al-Thurayyā, al-Dabarān, or al-Simāk”; they were forbidden to say this. Lisān al-ʿArab, roots n-w-ʾ and s-m-k.
notes.ar: السماك نجم معروف، والنوء النجم إذا مال للمغيب، وكانوا في الجاهلية يقولون: مطرنا بنوء الثريا والدبران والسماك. فنهوا عن ذلك. اللسان (ن و أ)، (س م ك).

notes.en: Ṣāʿiqah is a fire falling from the sky amid intense thunder. Lisān al-ʿArab, root ṣ-ʿ-q. See the discussion of its meaning above, 1/690–691.
notes.ar: الصاعقة: نار تسقط من السماء في رعد شديد. اللسان (ص ع ق). وينظر ما تقدم في معناها 1/ 690، 691.

notes.en: Najdah means hardship. A man described as najud or najid is hardy and courageous; najad can also mean sweat from exertion or distress. Lisān al-ʿArab, root n-j-d. Al-Suyūṭī attributed the report in al-Durr al-manthūr 4/48–49 to the author and Abū al-Shaykh.
notes.ar: النجدة: الشدة، ورجل نَجُد ونَجِد: شديد البأس، والنَّجَد: العرق من عمل أو كرب. اللسان (ن ج د). والأثر عزاه السيوطي في الدر المنثور 4/ 48، 49 إلى المصنف وأبى الشيخ.

notes.en: Al-Mufaḍḍaliyyāt, p. 121, and its commentary, p. 227. Kuss is the plural of akass, a hoof worn down through heavy trampling. Sunbuk is the front tip and sides of the hoof. Lisān al-ʿArab, roots k-s-s and s-n-b-k.

notes.en: Ibn Abī Shaybah transmitted it 10/214, 216 through two chains from Jaʿfar ibn Burqān as a mursal report. Aḥmad 10/47–48 (no. 5763), al-Bukhārī in al-Adab al-mufrad (no. 721), al-Tirmidhī (no. 3450), al-Nasāʾī in al-Kubrā (nos. 10763–10764), and others transmitted it as a raised report from Ibn ʿUmar.
notes.ar: أخرجه ابن أبي شيبة 10/ 214، 216 من طريقين عن جعفر بن برقان به مرسلًا. وأخرجه أحمد 10/ 47، 48 (5763)، والبخارى في الأدب المفرد (721)، والترمذى (3450)، والنسائى في الكبرى (10763، 10764)، وغيرهم من حديث ابن عمر مرفوعًا.

notes.en: Ibn Mardawayh transmitted it in his Tafsīr (as cited in al-Zaylaʿī’s Takhrīj al-Kashshāf 2/184) through ʿAttāb ibn Ziyād, from a man, from Abū Hurayrah, as a raised report.
notes.ar: أخرجه ابن مردويه في تفسيره - كما في تخريج الكشاف للزيلعى 2/ 184 - من طريق عتاب بن زياد عن رجل، عن أبي هريرة مرفوعا.

notes.en: Al-Suyūṭī attributed it in al-Durr al-manthūr 4/50 to Ibn Abī al-Dunyā in Kitāb al-maṭar, Ibn al-Mundhir, and al-Kharāʾiṭī in Makārim al-akhlāq.

notes.en: Qiḥf is the bone above the brain inside the skull. It is also said that a man’s qiḥf is the fragment split off from his skull and detached; it is not called a qiḥf until it separates. Lisān al-ʿArab, root q-ḥ-f.
notes.ar: القِحفُ: العظمُ الذي فوق الدماغ من الجمجمة، والجمجمة التي فيها الدماغ، وقيل: قحف الرجل: ما انفلق من جمجمته، فبان، ولا يدعى قحفا حتى يبين. لسان العرب (ق ح ف).

notes.en: Al-Kharāʾiṭī transmitted it in Makārim al-akhlāq (as cited in Abū Ṭāhir al-Silafī’s selection from it, p. 234, no. 568) through Abān ibn Yazīd.

notes.en: He is Maymūn ibn Qays, known as al-Aʿshā al-Kabīr. The verse appears in his Dīwān, p. 7; Majāz al-Qurʾān 1/325; and Lisān al-ʿArab, root m-ḥ-l.

notes.en: Nabʿ is a hard wood used to make bows and arrows from its branches; it grows on the summit of a mountain. Nadā means generosity; miḥāl means punishment and plotting. Dīwān al-Aʿshā al-Kabīr, p. 7; al-Wasīṭ, root q-l-l.
notes.ar: النبعُ: شجر صلب تتخذ منه القِسيُّ ومن أغصانه السهام، ينبت في قُلة الجبل: أي أعلاه. والندى: الكرم، والمحال: العقوبة والمكر. ديوان الأعشى الكبير ص 7، والوسيط (ق ل ل).

Ibn Ḥibbān transmitted it (no. 6450) through Muʿāwiyah ibn Sallām. Aḥmad 29/191 (no. 17642), Ibn Abī ʿĀṣim in al-Sunnah (no. 716), al-Ṭabarānī in al-Kabīr 17/128, and Ibn ʿAbd al-Barr in al-Tamhīd 3/320 transmitted it through Yaḥyā ibn Kathīr, from ʿĀmir ibn Zayd. All of them except Aḥmad have “ʿAmr ibn Zayd” instead of “ʿĀmir.” Al-Suyūṭī attributed it in al-Durr al-manthūr 4/59 to Ibn Abī Ḥātim and Ibn Mardawayh.

notes.en: Al-Suyūṭī attributed it in al-Durr al-manthūr 4/63 to the author and Ibn al-Anbārī in al-Maṣāḥif. Al-Zamakhsharī, in al-Kashshāf 2/360, rejects this and similar claims as incompatible with the Qurʾān’s preservation and transmission. Al-Qurṭubī likewise calls the attribution to Ibn ʿAbbās false, noting that Mujāhid and Saʿīd ibn Jubayr reported Ibn ʿAbbās reciting the wording found in the codex.
notes.ar:
عزاه السيوطي في الدر المنثور 4/ 63 إلى المصنف وابن الأنباري في المصاحف. وقال الزمخشري في الكشاف 2/ 360: وهذا ونحوه مما لا يصدق في كتاب الله الذي لا يأتيه الباطل من بين يديه ولا من خلفه، وكيف يخفى مثل هذا حتى يبقى ثابتا بين دفتي الكتاب وكان متقلبا في أيدى أولئك الأعلام المحتاطين في دين الله 
…. هذه واللَّه فرية ما فيها مرية. وقال القرطبي في تفسيره 9/ 320: وهو باطل عن ابن عباس؛ لأن مجاهدا وسعيد بن جبير حكيا الحرف عن ابن عباس على ما هو في المصحف.

notes.en: Ibn Abī Ḥātim transmitted it through ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ṣāliḥ (as cited in al-Itqān 2/22). Al-Suyūṭī attributed it in al-Durr al-manthūr 4/63 to Ibn al-Mundhir.

notes.ar: أخرجه اللالكائى في شرح اعتقاد أهل السنة (975) من طريق شريك، عن عطاء، عن مجاهد به.

notes.ar: أخرجه الحاكم في المستدرك 2/ 349 من طريق حماد به وعزاه السيوطي في الدر المنثور 4/ 65 إلى محمد بن نصر وابن المنذر وابن أبي حاتم.

notes.en: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Aḥmad transmitted it in Zawāʾid al-zuhd, p. 358; through him, Abū Nuʿaym in Ḥilyat al-awliyāʾ 4/104, through ʿUthām.
notes.ar: أخرجه عبد الله بن أحمد في زوائد الزهد ص 358، ومن طريقه أبو نعيم في الحلية 4/ 104، من طريق عثام به.

notes.en: Ṣ, T1, T2, and F read: “ibn Ḥakīmah”; M reads: “ibn Abī Ḥakīmah.” The adopted form is correct, as shown by the following report and the sources cited for it. See al-Jarḥ wa-l-taʿdīl 7/20 and al-Thiqāt 7/298.
notes.ar: في ص، ت 1، ت 2، ف: "بن حكيمة"، وفى م: "بن أبي حكيمة". والمثبت هو الصواب كما في الأثر التالي ومصادر التخريج، وينظر الجرح والتعديل 7/ 20، والثقات 7/ 298.

notes.en: Al-Bukhārī transmitted it in al-Tārīkh al-kabīr 7/63 through Abū ʿĀmir; al-Dūlābī transmitted it in al-Kunā 1/155 through Qurrah. Al-Suyūṭī attributed it in al-Durr al-manthūr to ʿAbd ibn Ḥumayd and Ibn al-Mundhir.
notes.ar: أخرجه البخارى في التاريخ الكبير 7/ 63 من طريق أبي عامر به، وأخرجه الدولابي في الكنى 1/ 155 من طريق قرة به، وعزاه السيوطي في الدر المنثور إلى عبد بن حميد وابن المنذر.

notes.en: Ibn Saʿd transmitted it in al-Ṭabaqāt 3/574 from ʿAffān. Al-Ḥārith transmitted it in his Musnad (as cited in al-Maṭālib, no. 4024), and Ibn ʿAdī 6/2131 through Hammām. Al-Ḥāfiẓ attributed it in al-Iṣābah 1/434 to Ibn Shāhīn and Ibn Mardawayh.
notes.ar: أخرجه ابن سعد في الطبقات 3/ 574 عن عفان به، وأخرجه الحارث في مسنده - كما في المطالب (4024) - وابن علي 6/ 2131 من طريق همام به، وعزاه الحافظ في الإصابة 1/ 434 إلى ابن شاهين وابن مردويه.

notes.en: Al-Ḥāfiẓ cited a similar report in Fatḥ al-bārī 11/309 from Abū Ṣāliḥ, then said it is weak because it comes through al-Kalbī, who is extremely weak.
notes.ar: ذكر الحافظ في الفتح 11/ 309 نحوه عن أبي صالح، ثم قال: لكنه ضعيف من رواية الكلبي، وهو ضعيف جدًّا.

notes.en: Abū ʿUbayd transmitted it in his Nāsikh, p. 5, and Ibn al-Jawzī in al-Nawāsikh, p. 85, through ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ṣāliḥ. Ibn Abī Ḥātim also transmitted it through him (as cited in Taghlīq al-taʿlīq 5/380 and Fatḥ al-bārī 13/523), but with different wording, as noted above. Al-Suyūṭī attributed it in al-Durr al-manthūr 4/67 to Ibn al-Mundhir and al-Bayhaqī in al-Madkhal.
notes.ar: أخرجه أبو عبيد في ناسخه ص 5، وابن الجوزى في النواسخ ص 85، من طريق عبد الله بن صالح به، وقد أخرجه ابن أبي حاتم - كما في تغليق التعليق 5/ 380، وفتح البارى 13/ 523 - من طريق عبد الله بن صالح به، لكن بلفظ مختلف كما سبق هنا. وعزاه السيوطي في الدر المنثور 4/ 67 إلى ابن المنذر والبيهقي في المدخل.

notes.en: Al-Suyūṭī attributed it in al-Durr al-manthūr 4/67 to the author.
notes.ar: عزاه السيوطي في الدر المنثور 4/ 67 إلى المصنف.

notes.en: Ṣ adds after it: “He said: God causes His Prophet to forget whatever He wills, abrogates whatever He wills, and confirms whatever He wills.”
notes.ar: بعده في ص: "قال: ينسى الله نبيه ما يشاء وينسخ ما يشاء ويثبت ما يشاء".

notes.en: Ibn Kathīr cited it in his Tafsīr 4/390 and 5/100 from the author. Al-Dārimī transmitted it in al-Radd ʿalā al-jahmiyyah, p. 32, and Ibn Khuzaymah in al-Tawḥīd, p. 98, through Ibn Abī Maryam. Al-Bazzār (no. 3516, Kashf edition), Ibn Abī Shaybah in al-ʿArsh, p. 86, Ibn Khuzaymah, p. 90, al-ʿUqaylī 2/93, al-Ṭabarānī in al-Awsaṭ (no. 8635) and al-Duʿāʾ (no. 135), al-Dāraquṭnī 3/1151–1152, and Ibn al-Jawzī in al-ʿIlal al-mutanāhiyah 1/25 transmitted it through al-Layth. Ibn Kathīr notes an addition unique to this version; al-Haythamī says it contains Ziyādah ibn Muḥammad al-Anṣārī, whose reports are rejected.
notes.ar: ذكره ابن كثير في تفسيره 4/ 390، 5/ 100 عن المصنف، وأخرجه الدارمي في الرد على الجهمية ص 32، وابن خزيمة في التوحيد ص 98 من طريق ابن أبي مريم به، وأخرجه البزار (3516 - كشف)، وابن أبى شيبة في العرش ص 86، وابن خزيمة ص 90، والعقيلى 2/ 93، والطبري في الأوسط (8635) وفى الدعاء (135)، والدارقطني في المؤتلف 3/ 1151، 1152، وابن الجوزى في العلل المتناهية 1/ 25 من طريق الليث به، وقال ابن كثير في تفسيره 5/ 100 تفرد به زيادة، وقال الهيثمي: وفيه زيادة بن محمد الأنصاري، وهو منكر الحديث.

notes.en: Al-Zaylaʿī cited it in Takhrīj al-Kashshāf 2/80 from the author. Ibn Mardawayh transmitted it through Ādam (as cited there). Al-Suyūṭī attributed it in al-Durr al-manthūr 4/65 to Ibn Abī Ḥātim.
notes.ar: ذكره الزيلعي في تخريج الكشاف 2/ 80 عن المصنف، وأخرجه ابن مردويه - كما في تخريج الكشاف - من طريق آدم به، وعزاه السيوطي في الدر المنثور 4/ 65 إلى ابن أبي حاتم.

notes.en: Al-Bayhaqī transmitted it in al-Shuʿab (no. 3741) through al-Muʿtamir, and also (no. 3742) through Qays.
notes.ar: أخرجه البيهقي في الشعب (3741) من طريق المعتمر به، وأخرجه أيضًا (3742) من طريق قيس به.

notes.ar: أخرجه عبد الرزاق في التفسير 2/ 194، وأبو داود في ناسخه - ومن طريقه ابن حجر في تغليق التعليق 4/ 308 - من طريق معمر به.

notes.ar: عزاه السيوطي في الدر المنثور 4/ 68 إلى المصنف.

notes.en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq transmitted it in his Tafsīr 1/339 from Maʿmar. Al-Suyūṭī attributed it in al-Durr al-manthūr 4/68 to ʿAbd ibn Ḥumayd and Ibn Abī Ḥātim.
notes.ar: أخرجه عبد الرزاق في تفسيره 1/ 339 عن معمر به، وعزاه السيوطي في الدر المنثور 4/ 68 إلى عبد بن حميد وابن أبي حاتم.

notes.en: Omitted in T1, T2, and F.
notes.ar: سقط من: ت 1، ت 2، ف.

notes.en: Nuʿaym ibn Ḥammād transmitted it in al-Fitan 1/243 (no. 690), al-Ḥākim 2/350, and al-Khaṭīb in al-Faqīh wa-l-mutafaqqih (nos. 154–155), through Ṭalḥah, in an extended version. Al-Suyūṭī attributed it in al-Durr al-manthūr 4/68 to ʿAbd al-Razzāq, Ibn Abī Shaybah, Ibn al-Mundhir, and Ibn Abī Ḥātim.
notes.ar: أخرجه نعيم بن حماد في الفتن 1/ 243 (690)، والحاكم 2/ 350، والخطيب في الفقيه والمتفقه (154، 155) من طريق طلحة به. وعزاه السيوطي في الدر المنثور 4/ 68 إلى عبد الرزاق وابن أبي شيبة وابن المنذر وابن أبي حاتم.

notes.en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq transmitted a similar version in his Tafsīr 1/339 through another chain from Mujāhid. Al-Suyūṭī attributed it in al-Durr al-manthūr 4/68 to Ibn Abī Shaybah and the author.
notes.ar: أخرجه عبد الرزاق في تفسيره 1/ 339 من طريق آخر عن مجاهد بنحوه. وعزاه السيوطي في الدر المنثور 4/ 68 إلى ابن أبي شيبة والمصنف.

notes.en: Omitted in T1, T2, and F.
notes.ar: سقط من: ت 1، ت 2، ف.

notes.en: Omitted in M.
notes.ar: سقط من: م.

notes.en: Ṣ and T2 read: “they hear.”
notes.ar: في ص، ت 2: "يسمعون".

notes.en: Ṣ, T1, T2, and F read: “He will know.”
notes.ar: في ص، ت 1، ت،2 ف: "سيعلم".

notes.en: Ibn Kathīr, Nāfiʿ, and Abū ʿAmr read it this way. Ibn Mujāhid, The Seven Readings, p. 359; Ḥujjat al-qirāʾāt, p. 375; al-Taysīr, p. 109.
notes.ar: قرأ بذلك ابن كثير ونافع وأبو عمرو السبعة لابن مجاهد ص 359، وحجة القراءات ص 375، والتيسير ص 109.

notes.en: ʿĀṣim, Ibn ʿĀmir, Ḥamzah, and al-Kisāʾī read it this way. See the same sources.
notes.ar: قرأ بذلك عاصم وابن عامر وحمزة والكسائي. تنظر المصادر السابقة.

notes.en: Both readings are correct.
notes.ar: القراءتان كلتاهما صواب.

notes.en: Ibn Abī Dāwūd, al-Maṣāḥif, p. 63.
notes.ar: المصاحف لابن أبي داود ص 63.

notes.en: See al-Baḥr al-muḥīṭ 5/401. This is an irregular reading because it conflicts with the spelling of the codex.
notes.ar: ينظر البحر المحيط 5/ 401، وهى قراءة شاذة لمخالفتها رسم المصحف.

notes.en: Omitted in T1, T2, and F.
notes.ar: سقط من: ت 1 ت 2 ف.

notes.en: Al-Tirmidhī transmitted it (nos. 3256, 3803), as did al-Ājurrī in al-Sharīʿah (no. 1442), through ʿAlī ibn Saʿīd al-Kindī, in an extended version.
notes.ar: أخرجه الترمذى (3256)، (3803)، والآجرى في الشريعة (1442) من طريق على بن سعيد الكندى به مطولا.

notes.en: Al-Suyūṭī attributed it in al-Durr al-manthūr 4/69 to the author and Ibn Mardawayh.
notes.ar: عزاه السيوطي في الدر المنثور 4/ 69 إلى المصنف وابن مردويه.

notes.en: Al-Suyūṭī attributed it in al-Durr al-manthūr 4/69 to the author.
notes.ar: عزاه السيوطي في الدر المنثور 4/ 69 إلى المصنف.

notes.en: Al-Thawrī’s Tafsīr, p. 155. Ibn Saʿd transmitted it in al-Ṭabaqāt 2/353; through him, Ibn ʿAsākir 29/131, from al-Faḍl ibn Dukayn, from Sufyān, from a trustworthy man. Ibn ʿAsākir also transmitted it 29/131 through Ḥumayd al-Aʿraj, from Mujāhid. Al-Suyūṭī attributed it in al-Durr al-manthūr 4/69 to Ibn Abī Shaybah and Ibn al-Mundhir.
notes.ar: تفسير الثورى ص 155 وأخرجه ابن سعد في الطبقات 2/ 353، ومن طريقه ابن عساكر 29/ 131 عن الفضل بن دكين عن سفيان عن رجل ثقة به، وأخرجه أيضًا ابن عساكر 29/ 131 من طريق حميد الأعرج عن مجاهد به، وعزاه السيوطي في الدر المنثور 4/ 69 إلى ابن أبي شيبة وابن المنذر.

notes.en: Mujāhid’s Tafsīr, p. 409.
notes.ar: تفسير مجاهد ص 409.

notes.en: Omitted in Ṣ and F.
notes.ar: سقط من: ص، ف.

notes.en: The manuscripts read: “as.”
notes.ar: في النسخ: "كما".

notes.en: Al-Suyūṭī attributed it in al-Durr al-manthūr 4/69 to the author, ʿAbd al-Razzāq, Ibn al-Mundhir, and Ibn Abī Ḥātim.
notes.ar: عزاه السيوطي في الدر المنثور 4/ 69 إلى المصنف وعبد الرزاق وابن المنذر وابن أبي حاتم.

notes.en: Omitted from the manuscripts; this is a chain of transmission used repeatedly by the author.
notes.ar: سقط من النسخ، وهو سند دائر عند المصنف.

notes.en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq transmitted it in his Tafsīr 1/339 from Maʿmar.
notes.ar: أخرجه عبد الرزاق في تفسيره 1/ 339 عن معمر به.

notes.en: This is the reading of ʿAlī, Ubayy, Ibn ʿAbbās, ʿIkrimah, Ibn Jubayr, ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Abī Bakrah, al-Ḍaḥḥāk, Sālim ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUmar, Ibn Abī Isḥāq, Mujāhid, al-Ḥakam, and al-Aʿmash. See al-Baḥr al-muḥīṭ 5/402 and Mukhtaṣar shawādhdh al-qirāʾāt, p. 72.
notes.ar: هي قراءة على وأبيّ وابن عباس وعكرمة وابن جبير وعبد الرحمن بن أبى بكرة والضحاك وسالم بن عبد الله بن عمر وابن أبي إسحاق ومجاهد والحكم والأعمش. ينظر البحر المحيط 5/ 402، مختصر شواذ القراءات ص 72.

notes.en: Ṣ, F, and T2 read: “from.”
notes.ar: في ص، ف، ت 2: "عن".

notes.en: Al-Suyūṭī attributed it in al-Durr al-manthūr 4/69 to the author, Abū ʿUbayd, Ibn al-Mundhir, and Ibn Abī Ḥātim.
notes.ar: عزاه السيوطي في الدر المنثور 4/ 69 إلى المصنف وأبي عبيد وابن المنذر وابن أبي حاتم.

notes.en: Al-Suyūṭī attributed it in al-Durr al-manthūr 4/69 to the author, Ibn al-Mundhir, and Ibn Abī Ḥātim.
notes.ar: عزاه السيوطي في الدر المنثور 4/ 69 إلى المصنف وابن المنذر وابن أبي حاتم.

notes.en: Ṣ, T1, T2, and F add after it: “ibn Muḥammad,” which is an error. The intended person is the Basran, not al-Ḥasan ibn Muḥammad, the author’s teacher. This irregular reading was also recited by ʿAlī, along with al-Ḥasan and Ibn al-Sumayqiʿ. See al-Baḥr al-muḥīṭ 5/402 and Mukhtaṣar shawādhdh al-qirāʾāt, p. 72.
notes.ar: بعده في ص، ت 1، ت 2، ف: "بن محمد" وهو خطأ، فالمقصود البصرى، لا الحسن بن محمد شيخ المصنف، وهذه القراءة قرأ بها مع الحسن على رضي الله عنه وابن السميقع وهي شاذة. ينظر البحر المحيط 5/ 402 ومختصر شواذ القراءات ص 72.

notes.en: See ʿAbd al-Razzāq’s Tafsīr 1/339.
notes.ar: ينظر تفسير عبد الرزاق 1/ 339.

notes.en: Saʿīd ibn Manṣūr (no. 1177, Tafsīr section) and al-Naḥḥās in his Nāsikh, p. 536, transmitted it through Abū ʿAwānah. Al-Suyūṭī attributed it in al-Durr al-manthūr 4/69 to Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abī Ḥātim. This is an irregular reading.
notes.ar: أخرجه سعيد بن منصور (1177 - تفسير) والنحاس في ناسخه ص 536 من طريق أبي عوانة به، وعزاه السيوطي في الدر المنثور 4/ 69 إلى ابن المنذر وابن أبي حاتم وهي قراءة شاذة.

notes.en: Abū Yaʿlā transmitted it (no. 5574) through al-Zuhrī; Ibn ʿAdī 6/2278 transmitted it through Ibn ʿUmar, from ʿUmar. Al-Suyūṭī attributed it in al-Durr al-manthūr 4/69 to Ibn Mardawayh.
notes.ar: أخرجه أبو يعلى (5574) من طريق الزهرى به، وابن علي 6/ 2278 من طريق ابن عمر عن عمر به، وعزاه السيوطي في الدر المنثور 4/ 69 إلى ابن مردويه.

notes.en: M reads: “among those”; T1, T2, and F: “from.”
notes.ar: في م: "ممن"، وفى ت 1، ت 2، ف: "من".
